Senses.Explanation: Yao and Shun, the paired sage-kings whom the Chan corpus uses as its classical measure of rule and then repeatedly puts under further questioning. In the Ancestral Guidelines Collection, Qinshan Puchu calls a ruler “a ruler like Yao and Shun,” calls the people those of Cheng and Kang, and immediately asks for the song of peace. Another recurrent line says, “The old farmer does not know the power of Yao and Shun; thump, thump, he beats the drum and sacrifices to the river god.” In the Five Lamps Complete Collection, an unnamed monk recites that inherited line and Nantang Qingyu answers, “Eyes seeing as if blind; mouth speaking as if mute.” Other texts explicitly limit the pair. Xichan Shoujing says even a ruler like Yao and Shun still has transforming activity, then contrasts this with what heaven and earth cannot contain and what Yao and Shun do not know by name. Juelang Daosheng says, “A true son of heaven does not rely on decrees from Yao and Shun,” while his lineage verse reverses the wording before a whisk opens the crown-eye. In the Touzi–Furong case, Touzi Yiqing asks whether the ruler's command relies on Yu, Tang, Yao, or Shun; as Furong Daokai prepares to answer, Touzi Yiqing strikes him with the whisk and assigns twenty blows. In the question-and-answer record of Wunian Shenyou, Wunian Shenyou answers why people today cannot accomplish what Yao and Shun did. The Zen deviation is the pair's use inside the interview: ideal rulers become lines to answer, measures explicitly exceeded, and names inside a command question enforced with the teaching-seat whisk.
Senses.Note: Exact concordance: 383 matches in 146 allowlisted texts. “A ruler like Yao and Shun” occurs 51 times in 35 texts, “the power of Yao and Shun” 62/47, and “Yao and Shun do not know the name” 12/10. One paired-figure sense: court blessing, political comparison, public question, and critical contrast all invoke the same two sage-kings. Their individual names and the neighboring Yu-and-Tang pair are family items, not extra senses of the fixed pair.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Record of Juelang Daosheng (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄): Juelang Daosheng says a true son of heaven does not rely on decrees from Yao and Shun.

Occurrences.Kwic: 天子假敕堯舜無，一拂打開頂眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Record of Juelang Daosheng (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄): Juelang Daosheng's lineage verse reverses the command line and follows it with one whisk opening the crown-eye.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖然如是，堯舜之君猶有化在。爭似乾坤収不得，堯舜不知名。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linked Lamps Compendium (聯燈會要), Xichan Shoujing section: Xichan Shoujing says even a ruler like Yao and Shun has transforming activity, then contrasts what they do not know by name. Xichan Shoujing is not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：野老不知堯舜力，鼕鼕打鼓祭江神。師曰：眼見如盲，口說如啞。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Five Lamps Complete Collection (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), within Nantang Qingyu's section, an unnamed monk recites the old-farmer line about not knowing Yao and Shun's power; Nantang replies that eyes see as if blind and the mouth speaks as if mute without repeating the headword. All six attribution rungs leave the questioning monk personally unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 汝道寰中天子勅。還假禹湯堯舜也無。楷擬酬之。青以拂子摵之曰。汝發意來早有二十棒也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Continued Record of the Lamp (續傳燈錄), in Touzi Yiqing's section, records Touzi Yiqing asking whether the ruler's command relies on Yu, Tang, Yao, or Shun and striking Furong Daokai with the whisk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「堯舜幹的事業，今人如何幹不來？」師曰：「堯舜當初恁麼做，何嘗要是與不是？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Question-and-answer Record of Wunian Shenyou (黃蘗無念禪師復問): Wunian Shenyou answers why people today cannot accomplish Yao and Shun's work. Wunian Shenyou is not yet in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 君乃堯舜之君，俗乃成康之俗。使林下野夫不覺成太平曲。且作麼生是太平曲？
